## Purpose

Enrichment on MetSigDB sets (Phase 5) needs a link from each measured ion to
the metabolites in the sets. The previous identifier processing
(`preprocessing/03_feature_ids.Rmd`) checked the identifiers of each ion for
mutual compatibility (RaMP via MetaProViz), removed incompatible ones,
extended the rest with `traverse_ids()` and `equivalent_id()`, and matched
one identifier type to the prior knowledge (e.g. KEGG IDs to KEGG pathways).
This notebook asks:

1. What do the identifiers of an ion mean in the original annotation?
2. What did the previous processing change?
3. How many ions reach MetSigDB sets through OmniPath Metabo's own entity
   resolution, starting from the original identifiers, compared with
   matching on the KEGG ID?
4. How ambiguous is the link from ion to set?

**Decision supported:** how ions are linked to MetSigDB sets for enrichment.

## Inputs

- `data/derived/cancer-cell-lines/shorthouse_v1/01_lines.rds` (ion table as published, Dataset EV2)
- `data/derived/cancer-cell-lines/shorthouse_v1/03_features.rds` (output of the previous identifier processing)
- OmniPath Metabo database, default deployment of `metabo.figures` (dev5), read only: `identifier_evidence`, `entity_identifier_lookup`, `chemical_resolution_group_member`, `metsigdb_membership`

## Methods

Identifiers were normalised (HMDB to seven digits, whitespace removed). Each
HMDB and KEGG compound identifier was looked up in OmniPath Metabo and linked
to all entities carrying it. Entities describing the same structure were
merged with the database's chemical resolution groups at level 1 (the first
InChIKey block: connectivity, ignoring stereochemistry and protonation), since
flow-injection MS cannot separate stereoisomers; level 2 (adding
stereochemistry) is shown for comparison. For example, the two glutathione
entities that carry MetSigDB memberships differ only in charge and fall into
one group. Entities without an InChIKey (name-only records) keep their
memberships but do not count as a structure. A structure group belongs to a
set if any of its entities is a member. Pathway sets were restricted to human
(organism 9606); ClassyFire and MACdb sets have no organism.

For comparison, the KEGG route matches the ion's KEGG compound IDs to the
`kegg` column of the KEGG sets, as with the previous approach of matching one
identifier type to the prior knowledge.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# metabo.figures provides the database connection
pkgload::load_all(here::here(), export_all = FALSE, quiet = TRUE)
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/use_case.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/plotting.R"))
config <- load_config()
derived_dir <- uc_dir(config, "derived")
fig_dir <- uc_dir(config, "output", "audit_12_metabolite_identifiers")

original <- readRDS(file.path(derived_dir, "01_lines.rds"))$ions
processed <- readRDS(file.path(derived_dir, "03_features.rds"))

# split a ";"-separated field into trimmed values
split_ids <- function(x) lapply(strsplit(coalesce(x, ""), ";"), function(v) { v <- trimws(v); v[v != ""] })
# HMDB IDs in the current seven-digit form (HMDB01659 -> HMDB0001659); other values -> NA
normalise_hmdb <- function(x) {
    digits <- sub("^HMDB", "", toupper(x))
    ifelse(grepl("^[0-9]+$", digits), paste0("HMDB", formatC(as.integer(digits), width = 7, flag = "0")), NA_character_)
}
```

## 1. What the identifiers of an ion mean

```{r structure}
# one row per candidate: names and HMDB IDs are parallel lists
candidates <- original %>%
    transmute(ionIdx, names = split_ids(name), hmdb = split_ids(hmdb), kegg = split_ids(kegg)) %>%
    mutate(n_names = lengths(names), n_hmdb = lengths(hmdb), n_kegg = lengths(kegg))

c(ions = nrow(candidates),
  one_candidate = sum(candidates$n_names == 1),
  several_candidates = sum(candidates$n_names > 1),
  names_and_hmdb_parallel = sum(candidates$n_names == candidates$n_hmdb),
  without_kegg = sum(candidates$n_kegg == 0))
count(candidates, candidates = pmin(n_names, 10))

candidates %>% filter(n_names > 1) %>% head(8) %>%
    transmute(ionIdx, names = sapply(names, paste, collapse = "; "), hmdb = sapply(hmdb, paste, collapse = "; "))
```

## 2. What the previous processing changed

```{r previous}
# HMDB candidates per ion before and after, both normalised
hmdb_before <- candidates %>% select(ionIdx, hmdb) %>% unnest(hmdb) %>% mutate(hmdb = normalise_hmdb(hmdb))
hmdb_after <- processed %>% transmute(ionIdx, hmdb = split_ids(hmdb)) %>% unnest(hmdb) %>% mutate(hmdb = normalise_hmdb(hmdb))

change <- full_join(
    hmdb_before %>% group_by(ionIdx) %>% summarise(before = list(unique(hmdb)), .groups = "drop"),
    hmdb_after %>% group_by(ionIdx) %>% summarise(after = list(unique(hmdb)), .groups = "drop"),
    by = "ionIdx"
) %>%
    left_join(select(processed, ionIdx, compatibility = sub_tbl), by = "ionIdx") %>%
    mutate(removed = mapply(function(b, a) length(setdiff(b, a)), before, after),
           added = mapply(function(b, a) length(setdiff(a, b)), before, after))

change %>%
    group_by(compatibility) %>%
    summarise(ions = n(),
              ions_losing_candidates = sum(removed > 0), candidates_removed = sum(removed),
              ions_gaining_ids = sum(added > 0), ids_added = sum(added), .groups = "drop")

change %>%
    filter(removed > 0) %>%
    left_join(select(original, ionIdx, name), by = "ionIdx") %>%
    transmute(ionIdx, compatibility, name = substr(name, 1, 80), removed,
              removed_ids = mapply(function(b, a) paste(setdiff(b, a), collapse = "; "), before, after)) %>%
    preview_table(caption = "Ions that lost original HMDB candidates")
```

## 3. Link to MetSigDB through OmniPath Metabo

```{r resolve}
con <- pg_connect()
db_build <- build_manifest_for(con)
quote_list <- function(x) paste(DBI::dbQuoteString(con, unique(x)), collapse = ", ")

# original identifiers of all ions
id_table <- bind_rows(
    hmdb_before %>% filter(!is.na(hmdb)) %>% transmute(ionIdx, id_type = "HMDB", value = hmdb),
    candidates %>% select(ionIdx, kegg) %>% unnest(kegg) %>% filter(grepl("^C[0-9]{5}$", kegg)) %>%
        transmute(ionIdx, id_type = "KEGG", value = kegg)
) %>% distinct()

# identifiers -> entities
entities <- pg_query(con, sprintf("
    SELECT CASE WHEN t.name LIKE 'Hmdb%%' THEN 'HMDB' ELSE 'KEGG' END AS id_type, ie.value,
           l.entity_id::text AS entity_id
    FROM omnipath.identifier_evidence ie
    JOIN omnipath.vocab_identifier_type t USING (identifier_type_id)
    JOIN omnipath.entity_identifier_lookup l ON l.identifier_id = ie.identifier_id
    WHERE (t.name = 'Hmdb:OM:0004' AND ie.value IN (%s))
       OR (t.name = 'Kegg Compound:MI:2012' AND ie.value IN (%s))",
    quote_list(id_table$value[id_table$id_type == "HMDB"]),
    quote_list(id_table$value[id_table$id_type == "KEGG"])))

# entities -> structure groups; level 1 = InChIKey connectivity block (see specificity below)
structure_level <- 1
groups <- pg_query(con, sprintf("
    SELECT entity_id::text AS entity_id, group_key FROM omnipath.chemical_resolution_group_member
    WHERE level_id = %d AND entity_id::text IN (%s)", structure_level, quote_list(entities$entity_id)))
# entities without an InChIKey (name-only records) have no group: they keep their memberships
# for linking but do not count as a separate structure
entities <- entities %>% left_join(groups, by = "entity_id") %>% rename(structure = group_key)

# all entities of these structure groups
members <- pg_query(con, sprintf("
    SELECT group_key, entity_id::text AS entity_id FROM omnipath.chemical_resolution_group_member
    WHERE level_id = %d AND group_key IN (%s)", structure_level, quote_list(na.omit(groups$group_key))))
structure_entities <- distinct(transmute(members, structure = group_key, entity_id))

# MetSigDB memberships of these entities (human pathway sets; other set types have no organism)
membership <- pg_query(con, sprintf("
    SELECT resource, set_type, set_source_id, set_label, metabolite_entity_id::text AS entity_id
    FROM omnipath.metsigdb_membership
    WHERE metabolite_entity_id::text IN (%s) AND (organism = 9606 OR organism IS NULL)",
    quote_list(structure_entities$entity_id)))

# sets that list a KEGG compound ID of the data in their kegg column (all resources)
kegg_listed <- pg_query(con, sprintf("
    SELECT DISTINCT kegg AS value, resource, set_source_id FROM omnipath.metsigdb_membership
    WHERE (organism = 9606 OR organism IS NULL) AND kegg IN (%s)",
    quote_list(id_table$value[id_table$id_type == "KEGG"])))
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)

c(build_id = db_build$build_id,
  identifiers = nrow(id_table), resolved_identifiers = n_distinct(paste(entities$id_type, entities$value)),
  entities = n_distinct(entities$entity_id), structures = n_distinct(na.omit(entities$structure)))
```

### Specificity of the identifiers

```{r specificity}
# structures per identifier: generic identifiers (e.g. KEGG lipid classes) resolve to many
specificity <- entities %>%
    group_by(id_type, value) %>%
    summarise(structures = n_distinct(na.omit(structure)), .groups = "drop")
specificity %>%
    group_by(id_type) %>%
    summarise(identifiers = n(), no_structure = sum(structures == 0), one_structure = sum(structures == 1),
              two_to_five = sum(between(structures, 2, 5)),
              more_than_five = sum(structures > 5), max = max(structures), .groups = "drop")
specificity %>% arrange(desc(structures)) %>% head(10)

# for comparison: level 2 (connectivity + stereochemistry); level 1 merges stereoisomers,
# which the measurement cannot separate anyway
con <- pg_connect()
groups_level2 <- pg_query(con, sprintf("
    SELECT entity_id::text AS entity_id, group_key AS stereo FROM omnipath.chemical_resolution_group_member
    WHERE level_id = 2 AND entity_id::text IN (%s)", quote_list(entities$entity_id)))
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
entities %>%
    left_join(groups_level2, by = "entity_id") %>%
    group_by(id_type, value) %>%
    summarise(level1 = n_distinct(na.omit(structure)), level2 = n_distinct(na.omit(stereo)), .groups = "drop") %>%
    group_by(id_type) %>%
    summarise(one_structure_level1 = sum(level1 == 1), one_structure_level2 = sum(level2 == 1),
              several_level1 = sum(level1 > 1), several_level2 = sum(level2 > 1), .groups = "drop")
```

### Coverage under three linking rules

- **A, HMDB:** each candidate's HMDB ID, resolved to structures.
- **B, HMDB + specific KEGG:** A plus KEGG IDs that resolve to at most one structure.
- **C, B + listed KEGG:** B plus, for generic KEGG IDs, only the sets that list
  that KEGG compound ID themselves (no expansion to specific structures).
- *KEGG route (previous approach):* KEGG IDs matched to the kegg column of the KEGG sets.

```{r coverage}
pathway_resources <- c("KEGG", "Reactome", "WikiPathways")
structure_set <- structure_entities %>%
    inner_join(membership, by = "entity_id", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
    distinct(structure, resource, set_source_id)
specific_kegg <- specificity %>% filter(id_type == "KEGG", structures <= 1) %>% pull(value)
generic_kegg <- specificity %>% filter(id_type == "KEGG", structures > 1) %>% pull(value)

# ion -> identifier -> entities, plus all entities of their structures
ion_entities_rule <- function(kegg_values) {
    direct <- id_table %>%
        filter(id_type == "HMDB" | value %in% kegg_values) %>%
        inner_join(entities, by = c("id_type", "value"), relationship = "many-to-many")
    bind_rows(
        distinct(direct, ionIdx, entity_id, structure),
        direct %>% filter(!is.na(structure)) %>% distinct(ionIdx, structure) %>%
            inner_join(structure_entities, by = "structure", relationship = "many-to-many")
    ) %>% distinct()
}
ion_entities <- list(A = ion_entities_rule(character()), B = ion_entities_rule(specific_kegg))
ion_structure <- lapply(ion_entities, function(x) x %>% filter(!is.na(structure)) %>% distinct(ionIdx, structure))
ion_set <- lapply(ion_entities, function(x) x %>%
    inner_join(membership, by = "entity_id", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
    distinct(ionIdx, resource, set_source_id))
ion_set$C <- bind_rows(
    ion_set$B,
    id_table %>% filter(id_type == "KEGG", value %in% generic_kegg) %>%
        inner_join(kegg_listed, by = "value", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
        distinct(ionIdx, resource, set_source_id)
) %>% distinct()
ion_set$`KEGG route` <- id_table %>% filter(id_type == "KEGG") %>%
    inner_join(filter(kegg_listed, resource == "KEGG"), by = "value", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
    distinct(ionIdx, resource, set_source_id)

coverage <- bind_rows(lapply(names(ion_set), function(rule) {
    ion_set[[rule]] %>%
        group_by(resource) %>%
        summarise(ions = n_distinct(ionIdx), sets = n_distinct(set_source_id), .groups = "drop") %>%
        bind_rows(tibble(resource = "any pathway resource",
                         ions = n_distinct(ion_set[[rule]]$ionIdx[ion_set[[rule]]$resource %in% pathway_resources]),
                         sets = NA_integer_)) %>%
        mutate(rule = rule)
}))
coverage %>% select(rule, resource, ions) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = rule, values_from = ions)
```

```{r coverage-plot, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
rules <- c("A", "B", "C", "KEGG route")
p <- coverage %>%
    mutate(rule = factor(rule, levels = rules)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(ions, resource, fill = rule)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(preserve = "single")) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = nrow(original), linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = uc_palette(rules)) +
    labs(x = "Ions in at least one set (dashed: all ions)", y = NULL, fill = "Rule",
         title = "Ions linked to MetSigDB sets") +
    theme_uc()
save_figure(p, "coverage", fig_dir, width = 8, height = 4)
p
```

## 4. Ambiguity of the link

Under rule B: how many structures does an ion have, and are its pathway sets
shared by its candidates or contributed by one of them?

```{r ambiguity}
per_ion <- ion_structure$B %>% count(ionIdx, name = "structures")
summary(per_ion$structures)
count(per_ion, structures = pmin(structures, 6))

shared <- ion_structure$B %>%
    inner_join(structure_set %>% filter(resource %in% pathway_resources), by = "structure",
               relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
    group_by(ionIdx, set_source_id) %>%
    summarise(structures_in_set = n_distinct(structure), .groups = "drop") %>%
    left_join(per_ion, by = "ionIdx")
c(ion_set_pairs = nrow(shared),
  from_ions_with_one_structure = sum(shared$structures == 1),
  from_ambiguous_ions_all_candidates = sum(shared$structures > 1 & shared$structures_in_set == shared$structures),
  from_ambiguous_ions_one_candidate = sum(shared$structures > 1 & shared$structures_in_set == 1))

# ions with a single structure that are in at least one pathway set (rule B, and rule C)
unambiguous <- per_ion$ionIdx[per_ion$structures == 1]
c(unambiguous_ions = length(unambiguous),
  in_pathway_set_rule_B = n_distinct(intersect(unambiguous, ion_set$B$ionIdx[ion_set$B$resource %in% pathway_resources])),
  in_pathway_set_rule_C = n_distinct(intersect(unambiguous, ion_set$C$ionIdx[ion_set$C$resource %in% pathway_resources])))
```

## Interpretation

- **The identifiers of an ion are alternatives, not synonyms.** 577 of 1096
  ions are annotated with several candidate metabolites of the same mass
  (isomers or isobars, e.g. "Acetic acid; Glycolaldehyde"), and in 1093 ions
  the HMDB IDs run parallel to the candidate names, one per candidate.
- **The previous compatibility check therefore asks the wrong question.** It
  expects the identifiers of an ion to describe one compound, so ions with
  several candidates are "partially" or "completely incompatible" by design.
  The cleaning removed 1780 original HMDB candidates from 369 ions. For the
  completely incompatible ions it kept "the first" HMDB or KEGG ID, which
  depends on the order of the published list. The decision also rests on how
  complete the RaMP mapping is: a missing mapping looks like an
  incompatibility.
- **OmniPath Metabo resolves the original identifiers directly.** 4504 of
  4740 identifiers link to database entities. At InChIKey level 1, 3382 of
  3464 HMDB IDs resolve to exactly one structure. Most of the remaining
  ambiguity at level 2 is stereochemistry, which flow-injection MS cannot
  resolve anyway.
- **Generic KEGG IDs must not be expanded.** 124 KEGG IDs resolve to several
  structures, up to 846 for lipid classes (e.g. C00157 phosphatidylcholine,
  790 structures). At least one link is wrong: C00350
  (phosphatidylethanolamine) also links to hydroxyclomipramine, a drug
  metabolite. Rule C uses such IDs only for the sets that list the class
  compound itself.
- **Coverage is clearly better than matching on one ID type.** With rule C,
  719 ions are in at least one KEGG, Reactome or WikiPathways set, against
  529 with KEGG IDs alone (+36 %). KEGG covers 579 ions, Reactome 407,
  WikiPathways 604; MACdb covers 784 and ClassyFire 1095.
- **Ambiguity is the main remaining issue, and it is inherent to the data.**
  The 519 ions with one structure are exactly the ions with one candidate;
  306 of them are in a pathway set (rule C). For ions with several
  candidates, 7524 ion–set links rest on a single candidate and only 253 are
  shared by all candidates. Enrichment therefore has to handle ambiguity
  explicitly.

**Recommendations:**

1. Link ions to MetSigDB from the **original identifiers** (HMDB per
   candidate, KEGG), normalised, resolved through OmniPath Metabo at InChIKey
   level 1, with rule C for KEGG. The compatibility-based cleaning,
   `traverse_ids()` and `equivalent_id()` are not needed for this, since the
   database supplies the cross-references.
2. Decide how ambiguous ions enter enrichment (Phase 5).
3. Report C00350 → hydroxyclomipramine and the expansion of KEGG class IDs to
   the OmniPath Metabo developers.

sessionInfo()
